rejected_rule.statement: A deed of gift creating a fidei commissum can contain sufficient designation of beneficiaries if the words 'after their death' are construed as meaning after their deaths respectively, and the proper heirs are construed as though they read their proper heirs respectively.
rejected_rule.supporting_quote: "The words 'after their death' may, no doubt, mean 'after the death of all of them.' If the case of Fernando v. Fernando1 [ 127 N. L. R. 321. ] appears to support that contention, the case of Abeyeratne v. Jagarw 2 [ 226 N. L. R. 181. ] is even more strongly in support of the contention of counsel for the plaintiff' that the words 'after their death' should be construed as though they read 'after their deaths respectively' and that the concluding words 'their proper heirs' should be construed as though they read 'their proper heirs respectively,'"
